chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slave girl when she is divorced, what is her waiting period? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Two menstruations, or two months, until she menstruates.' I said, 'Supposing her husband dies from her?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) said regarding the mothers of the children: They should not get married until they observe the waiting period of four months and ten (days), and they are slaves.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period of a slave girl after divorce or death of husband
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the iddah for slave women, distinguishing between divorce (two menstruations or two months) and widowhood (four months and ten days). It highlights the scholarly consensus that while the widowhood period for slave women mirrors that of free women, the divorce period is often determined by menstruation cycles rather than a fixed lunar duration, reflecting practical juristic applications in Shia fiqh.
